evidence.text: The entry calls 很 a phonetic compound and identifies 艮 as its sound element. It reports the Shuowen readings “不聽從也” and “行難也,” preferring the latter as the original sense; it explains later obstruction/defiance senses through the notion of being unable to proceed. This is one dictionary’s analysis, not independent confirmation of the proposed semantic derivation.

evidence.text: The entry analyzes 很 as a phono-semantic compound: semantic 彳 plus phonetic 艮. It gives Zhengzhang Shangfang’s Old Chinese reconstructions (2003): 很 *ɡɯːnʔ and 艮 *kɯːns, alongside the Middle Chinese category and fanqie 胡墾. This supports a phonetic role, although the reconstructed forms differ in final and tone and should not be treated as identical pronunciations.

evidence.text: For Mandarin, 艮 is gèn in Hanyu Pinyin; the entry lists Zhengzhang (2003) Old Chinese *kɯːns. These data provide a same-system historical comparison with 很 *ɡɯːnʔ. They establish an approximate phonetic relationship in that reconstruction, not a modern Mandarin sound match, since modern readings are 很 hěn and 艮 gèn.

evidence.text: The dictionary records 很戾 as “fierce/violent and perverse” and cites “趙王之很戾無親” from Shiji, Zhang Yi biography. It also records a Song-dynasty sense of hard and brittle in Su Shi’s 思治論. evidence.source: Journal of Chinese Language and Literature Translation, Lim Gyunghee (2012), abstract page
evidence.text: The study’s abstract places the noncompliance sense in pre-Qin usage, a fierce/cruel adjective developing in Han usage, and adverbial usage emerging in Yuan and flourishing in Qing. It describes a grammaticalization path via 很/狠 plus adjectives, where the form acquired an adverbial modifying function. This is a distinct scholarly account from the Yuan 哏 language-contact proposal.
evidence.title: 汉语程度副词“很”的产生与发展

evidence.source: 语言研究, Wang Hang and Ge Pingping (2024), article page
evidence.text: The accessible abstract argues that modern degree-adverb 很 arose from Yuan northern Chinese–Mongolian contact, with Yuan adverb 哏 as its predecessor; it proposes that 哏 disappeared from Ming official writing while the usage persisted in northern speech, sometimes written 狠, and that 很 became the dedicated degree spelling in Qing usage. The page provides an abstract and detailed notes but states full text requires CNKI; treat the causal account as the authors’ proposal, not settled consensus.
evidence.title: 现代汉语程度副词“很”的来源及演变

evidence.source: 语言研究, Wang Hang and Ge Pingping (2024), article page notes
evidence.text: The accessible notes report that 元典章 has a Yuan degree-adverb example “哏不便当,” but the article page’s excerpted notes do not identify its precise document date or give an independently inspected manuscript image. The authors further argue that Yuan source witnesses use 哏 while later editions sometimes normalize it to 很; Ming examples are commonly written 狠; and Qing witnesses show mixed 很/狠 spelling. They note that the cited Yuan orthography distinction remains subject to textual transmission and editorial changes.
evidence.title: 现代汉语程度副词“很”的来源及演变

gaps: No directly inspected oracle-bone, bronze, or Warring States form for 很 was found. The available graphic evidence reaches the Shuowen small-seal account; no graphic corruption or replacement history for the whole graph is established.

The relationship between the Shuowen’s “not obeying,” “difficult to walk,” and “perverse” senses is not demonstrated by dated primary passages here. Shuowen gives them as glosses, while 字通 prefers 行難 as original; this remains source-specific analysis.

The transition from defiance/cruelty to degree adverb is contested. One scholarly abstract proposes internal grammaticalization of 很/狠 adjective constructions; another proposes Yuan contact and a degree adverb 哏 preceding later 很. The accessible pages do not permit independent testing of all examples or contact causation.

The 2024 article page notes 元典章 “哏不便当” but its full text requires CNKI access; exact date, manuscript/edition, passage context, and reading were not directly verified. The precise dating and nature of the first degree-adverb use therefore remain unresolved.
Some source search results and Ctext pages were inaccessible (403 or timeout); search-result text is identified as such and not treated as a fully checked primary page.

The existence of 艮 as a later phonetic element is supported independently of uncertainty about its oldest graphic referent. Its role here is phonetic, not a claim that 很 borrows the whole graph or borrows a word named after a depicted object.

The evidence for 很’s and 艮’s Old Chinese comparison is from Zhengzhang Shangfang (2003): *ɡɯːnʔ versus *kɯːns. No same-system alternative reconstruction was checked in an opened specialist source during this search.
